terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: ONE BAY of a modular outdoor roof kit, and the only one of the five whose ROOF SURFACE is real geometry: a 4 x 4 m cell on a 4 m grid, four whole-bamboo corner posts, and a roof of split culms laid alternately hollow-up and hollow-down as interlocking tiles. Nothing opens, turns or swings and nothing attaches -- a neighbouring bay is PLACED at 4 m, not socketed -- so one root pivot at base-center and zero sockets. Open on all four sides. Garden shelters, farm sheds, beach bars and temple fair stalls; the cheapest roof in the kit and the one a village builds itself. Culms weather from green through cream to grey and are tied, never nailed.

reasoning: ONE bamboo merge -- four posts, eight head rails on two levels, two king culms, the ridge pole, five rafters and the capping culm -- ONE rope merge of forty lashing collars, and TWO InstancedMeshes for the roof (17 channels, 16 caps): FOUR draw calls of 4.

Each roof geometry carries BOTH slopes (a culm on +Z and one on -Z) so each set varies in x alone. Channels and caps are SEPARATE sets because the plate's green, cream and grey strips are independent of their neighbours: one pair geometry (the first build) forced every cap to share its channel's tone.

Three materials of three: bamboo (vertex colours -- two culm tones and the rafters), split bamboo (WHITE, because setColorAt multiplies, with eight channel and eight cap tones carried per instance) and rope (vertex colours -- two rope tones and black cord). All textureless, each with one canvas after construction.
The roof is 1,320 of the 3,480 triangles and the lashings 1,280; 87% of the budget, which is the registry notes' own prediction that this module would sit nearest its ceiling.
Action readiness: one root pivot, zero sockets, no declared collider shape, no destruction groups.

specDepthDecision.rationale: The identity is the alternating half-pipe course, and the notes say so: a run of half-cylinders reads wrong when it is flat, because the silhouette at the eave is a scalloped edge and not a line. That scallop is 33 open culm mouths, and it is the one place in the set where triangles buy something a canvas cannot.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedUnknowns: The roof stops ON the module edge (1.990 / 1.970) and the FRAME is inset 0.23 m under it: a bay that overhangs the cell collides with its neighbour, and a roof flush with its posts is not what the plate shows.

The half-pipes are single-thickness SHELLS on a double-sided material, not walled tubes. A hollow-up channel is seen from the inside at every azimuth, and a real wall would triple the roof's triangles for 8 mm nobody resolves at prop distance; the scallop at the eave, which is what the notes actually ask for, is the shell's own open mouth.
Ten segments per half culm on a 233 mm pitch, 40 triangles per culm; 66 culms are 1,320 triangles. The plate's eave shows 13-15 scallops across the bay, not 33.

The cap culm (r 0.12) sits half a pitch across with its axis 80 mm BELOW the channel axes, so its arc passes 36 mm over the two rims it bridges and its own rims hang 5 mm above the channel walls -- a real cap rests on the rims, and at this pitch the geometry that does so is one whose axis is lower, not higher.

Rope lashings are short thick collars concentric with the poles they bind, on a laid-strand tile; the X of a real square lashing is under a centimetre of relief at prop distance and the collar mass is what the plate shows.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 4.00 x 3.10 x 4.00 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=4000 triangles, <=4 draw calls, <=3 materials, <=6 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot plus 0 named mechanism pivot(s); zero sockets; none collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The rigid body of the prop at its declared origin. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it, and only real mechanisms get one.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.
actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center, +Y up, the ridge along X. A neighbouring bay sits at +-4.00 m on X or Z with the same alignment, and the two bays' corner posts then pair at the shared edge.

silhouette.description: A 4.00 x 4.00 m bay: four 160 mm bamboo posts at +-1.68 under a DOUBLE head rail at 2.03 and 2.27 m whose ends run 0.19 m past the posts, a ridge pole on two king culms, five rafters, and a low gable of 17 hollow-up split channels (r 0.085) on a 233 mm pitch with 16 hollow-down caps (r 0.12) bridging their rims, from a 2.40 m eave overhanging the frame by 0.23 m to a 3.10 m capping culm. Rope lashings at every joint. The eave is 17 open culm mouths, not a line. Open on all four sides.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x and z span -1.998..+1.998, set by the rope collars at the post heads: the post surface is already at 1.988 and a 66 mm collar radius crossed the cell edge at 2.004 on the first build, so the collars are 60 mm. y 0.000 to 3.100 at the crown of the capping culm -- which is r cos(PI/10) above its centre, not r, because a 10-segment cylinder has a flat there; centring it at H - r left the declared height 3.4 mm short. The roof culms were shortened 60 mm from the true rake: a cylinder rotated onto the slope has a z extent of half-L cos(s) + r sin(s), and at 40 mm short the cap culms reached 1.9974 against the frame collars' 1.9980 -- inside check-coplanar's 1 mm tolerance, and it reported all 66 pairs. On this bay the FRAME owns the z plane; on the two thatched ones the roof does. Proxy (Meshy v7): w:h:d 1 : 0.760 : 1.119, post grid 1.182 x 1.360 H, roof reaching 1.450 H at an eave sitting at 0.42 of the height -- a squat table of a shelter, which is what the plate shows. The notes fix a 2.40 eave under a 3.10 ridge, so the built bay is far taller in proportion and the roof is 23% of its height against the proxy's 58%. The proxy IS used for the culm diameter and for confirming the ridge runs across the narrow axis.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate: w:h:d 1 : 0.760 : 1.119, post grid 1.182 x 1.360 H, roof 1.450 H, eave at 0.42 H, 39-degree pitch. Used for the culm diameter and for confirming the ridge axis. NOT used for the proportions: the plate is a squat stand-in and the notes fix a 4 x 4 m bay at 2.40/3.10.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.92: the bay is symmetric about both axes and open on all four sides; the plate shows one gable end and one full slope.

repetitionSystems.name: Split bamboo channels, hollow up
repetitionSystems.placement: 17 instances on a 233 mm pitch across x from -1.885 to 1.885. Each instance is TWO half culms, one per slope: a hollow-up channel r 0.085, open-ended, theta length PI, ten segments, from z 0.06 under the capping culm to the eave tip at 1.990 on a 15.6 degree rake. Eight tones ride on the instance colour attribute.
repetitionSystems.notes: Both slopes are baked into the geometry so the set varies in x alone. Which half of each shell is material follows from the rotation: rotateX(PI/2 + s) sends local +Z downward on the +Z slope, so a channel is theta start -PI/2, and it flips on the -Z slope.

repetitionSystems.name: Split bamboo caps, hollow down
repetitionSystems.placement: 16 instances half a pitch across from the channels. Each is TWO hollow-down half culms r 0.120 with their axes 80 mm below the channel axes, from z 0.13 to 1.975, theta start +PI/2 on the +Z slope. Eight tones on the instance colour attribute, independent of the channels.
repetitionSystems.notes: A separate set so a cap's tone is independent of the channel under it, which is what the plate's unordered green / cream / grey strips need; two draw calls for the roof against one is the whole cost.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93. 3,480/4,000 triangles, 4/4 draw calls, 3/3 materials, 4/6 unique geometries, two 512 px and one 256 px canvas. lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the large class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Two components plus two repetition systems: 4 of 4. The second roof set buys independent cap tones and the rope merge buys a real lashing; both are the plate.

materials.note: bamboo, split and rope: 3 of 3. Culm and rope tones are vertex colours; the roof's sixteen tones are per-instance.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 3,480 of 4,000: 880 in the frame merge (22 cylinders at 8 or 10 segments), 1,280 in forty rope collars, 1,320 in the roof (66 open ten-segment half culms at 20 triangles each over two sets). 87% of the budget, which is the registry notes' own prediction for this module.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: Cylinders throughout: closed for the frame poles, open partial cylinders (theta length PI) for the roof shells and the lashing collars.
Two InstancedMeshes -- 17 channels and 16 caps -- each carrying both slopes. In a scene the HOST places whole bays on the 4 m grid.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.
All three materials are declared textureless. Two 512 px canvases (culm, split) and one 256 px rope canvas after construction, ~2.3 MB of texture VRAM.

risks.description: The half-pipes are shells with no wall thickness, on a double-sided material.
risks.mitigation: A walled culm triples the roof's triangles for 8 mm nobody resolves at prop distance, and the scallop the notes ask for is the shell's own open mouth. Double-sided is not optional here: a hollow-up channel is seen from the inside at every azimuth.

risks.description: The plate's roof is pitched near 25 degrees; the notes' 2.40 eave under a 3.10 ridge over a 2 m half-span, with the culms overhanging the frame, gives 15.6.
risks.mitigation: The eave and ridge are the module contract; the overhang, the culm width and the scallop are what the plate is judged on and all three are built.

risks.description: The proxy is a squat table with the eave at 0.42 H; the notes fix 2.40 under 3.10, which makes the roof 23% of the height against the proxy's 58%.
risks.mitigation: The notes are the module contract and the plate is a stand-in. The proxy IS used for the culm diameter and the ridge axis; arithmetic in envelopeDerivation.

risks.description: The collider derivation takes no rectangle under 0.15 m in both axes, and the first build's 100 mm posts fell through to a bounding-box block over the whole bay.
risks.mitigation: Posts are 160 mm now, above the minimum, and the fallback split into connected components (scripts/lib/colliders.mjs) stands behind that. The compound is re-derived and measured on promote.

risks.description: Open on all four sides, and the eave is 17 open culm mouths, so a lot of what the silhouette encloses is background.
risks.mitigation: Turntable run with --allow-holes; holeviz read per azimuth on this build: 5,088 / 28,386 / 5,047 / 28,379 enclosed px at 0/90/180/270, all of it the volume under the roof between the posts and rails and the gable voids -- no solid surface is classified as backdrop, the darkest solid face being the cord at luma 67 with sat 0.49.
